schemes.name: sangok_c04_develop_perforated_base
schemes.secondary_language: Perforated base beneath a continuous upper body
schemes.formal_principle: Lift a narrow transverse strip of the underside to form a covered ground passage through the central body and rear wall. The continuous upper volume frames the two carved courts while the retained north and south masses remain grounded.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Perforated base beneath a continuous upper body
schemes.reference_basis: Exact scored comp04 parent; architectural massing development. Public-office and meeting uses remain hypotheses.

ops.why: Retain the parent two-storey, 7.8 m maximum envelope and 3.9 m authored storey height.

design_argument_ko.title: Perforated base beneath a continuous upper body
design_argument_ko.spatial_strategy: Lift a narrow transverse strip of the underside to form a covered ground passage through the central body and rear wall. The continuous upper volume frames the two carved courts while the retained north and south masses remain grounded.
design_argument_ko.tradeoff: The passage is a modeled void, not a verified door, circulation route or engineered transfer structure. Its upper bridge needs structural development.

schemes.name: sangok_c04_develop_thickened_middle
schemes.secondary_language: Thickened central volume with a stepped section
schemes.formal_principle: Thicken the central occupied body between the two voids from 18 to 27 percent of the authored width, giving the common volume usable depth. Keep its roof at 7.8 m and lower the outer room bands slightly to distinguish the shared interior in section.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Thickened central volume with a stepped section

design_argument_ko.title: Thickened central volume with a stepped section
design_argument_ko.spatial_strategy: Thicken the central occupied body between the two voids from 18 to 27 percent of the authored width, giving the common volume usable depth. Keep its roof at 7.8 m and lower the outer room bands slightly to distinguish the shared interior in section.
design_argument_ko.tradeoff: Both courts give area to the deeper common body. The upper outer rooms have a lower envelope; room partitions and headroom below structural members are not yet designed.

schemes.name: sangok_c04_develop_rear_opening
schemes.secondary_language: Narrow rear opening between retained room masses
schemes.formal_principle: Cut a narrow full-height opening through the rear enclosing wall, giving the smaller court a direct rear address toward the mapped river-side context. The two room masses frame this slot while the broad opposite recess remains the primary public address.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Narrow rear opening between retained room masses

design_argument_ko.title: Narrow rear opening between retained room masses
design_argument_ko.spatial_strategy: Cut a narrow full-height opening through the rear enclosing wall, giving the smaller court a direct rear address toward the mapped river-side context. The two room masses frame this slot while the broad opposite recess remains the primary public address.
design_argument_ko.tradeoff: The quiet court becomes a sheltered pocket rather than a fully enclosed void. The mapped river-side relation does not establish a public access right or an existing pedestrian connection.

design_argument_ko.title: Recessed entry volume on the open court
design_argument_ko.spatial_strategy: Carve a deeper threshold into the southern occupied band facing the broad public recess. The retained wall returns frame an identifiable address for a meeting-room hypothesis while the central body and smaller court remain intact.
design_argument_ko.tradeoff: The recess consumes part of the southern room depth. It provides an architectural threshold, but night-time separation, doors, stairs and accessible routes remain unverified.
